claim: The filter a stereo flanger puts in front of itself and the filter a stereo chorus puts in front of itself are one section. Swept at every setting the chorus's was published at -- 15 of them across the two filter shapes the byte beside it offers -- the two types return the same skirt over a hundred and thirteen twelfth-octave bands to a median of 0.08 dB at worst, where those runs repeat themselves to 0.08 dB and where one step of the byte being swept moves the profile by at least 0.15 dB. The agreement is at the floor and the thing it is being told from is two to ten times the floor, so this is the reading saying the same section twice and not the reading running out. The page prints the two types' parameter lists identically -- same order, same addresses, same ranges -- with one entry in the flanger's that the chorus has not got, a feedback level in the slot the chorus leaves empty. That list is what made the question worth asking and it is not what answers it; what this file claims is the front end, and what the loop is around is queued.

measurements.why: The flanger's pre-filter through the low pass, with the loop opened, the modulator parked and the balance at all-effect.
The chorus's, published earlier, on the same grid at the same settings.
The flanger's through the high pass, which is the second shape the byte beside the cutoff offers and a different skirt to agree on.
The chorus's through the high pass.

The flanger's rate byte. Carried for the one setting where the two records disagree, and not as evidence that they are one structure -- the rate table is shared by nineteen types and cannot say anything about two of them in particular.
The chorus's rate byte, whose setting-32 reading rests on two of four takes and lands off the grid the rate class closed on.

document_rows.why: Both parameter lists in full, because the claim's second sentence is about them and a reader has to be able to see that the difference is one row. They are evidence about a page and nothing else; the section is read off the skirts.

era_priors.claim: A chorus and a flanger on a fixed-point part of this period are the same arithmetic: a short modulated delay summed with the dry signal, with the flanger differing by a path from the delay's output back to its input. Writing them as two stages costs two copies of the interpolator and the modulator for one extra multiply-accumulate of difference.
era_priors.why: It says why one front end being shared is worth reading as the two types being one stage rather than as two stages that happen to filter alike. It carries none of the claim: what is claimed is the section the measurement reached.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The two front ends had differed. They did not, at fifteen settings across two filter shapes, by more than the runs repeat themselves.

adds: Each record says what one type's pre-filter byte does to a band profile. What is read out of the pair is that the two profiles are the same profile -- a comparison between records, made against a third figure neither record states, which is what one step of the swept byte is worth under the same reading.

through the low pass.where_the_widest_figures_sit: Every one of them below about forty hertz, which is the bottom of the band set and where a held note has least energy to put in a band. The medians are taken over all of it and are two orders under the widest.

through the high pass.where_the_widest_figures_sit: Every one of them below about forty hertz, which is the bottom of the band set and where a held note has least energy to put in a band. The medians are taken over all of it and are two orders under the widest.

the_rate_byte_on_both.why_this_is_not_evidence_here: One table serves nineteen types, which is a closed claim of this archive's own. Two types returning the same entry of a table that every type returns entries of says nothing about those two being one structure, and it is set down here because leaving it out would look like it had been avoided.
the_rate_byte_on_both.what_it_is_good_for: A ruler. At setting 32 the two records disagree by 7.3 per cent, which is the one figure in this file that does not agree -- and the chorus's reading there rests on two of its four takes, with a third of them returning the flanger's value exactly. The rate table's own step settles it without another run: where that step is a twentieth of a hertz the flanger's 1.65 lands 0.0 steps off an entry and the chorus's 1.7799 lands 0.4 off the nearest one there is. A reading off the grid the class already closed on is a misread, not a second table -- and at the other three settings both types land within 0.03 of a step of an entry, each measured against the step its own region of the table has.

what_the_two_runs_held_differently: The flanger's run held `40 03 08` at 64, which is the centre of a range printed `-98% - +98%` and is the loop opened. The chorus has no such address, so there was nothing to match; the comparison is of a flanger with no feedback against a chorus.

The flanger's run held `40 03 09` Phase at 0 and the chorus's run left it where the unit powers it up. Both runs held the modulator's depth at 0, so there was no modulation for a phase between two modulators to be a phase of.

alternatives.reading: Two separate filter sections written from one specification, rather than one section reached from two types.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: Not applicable. The two readings predict the same output at every setting of every byte, so no sensitivity would help.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Nothing leaving this unit's sockets distinguishes one routine called from two places from two routines computing the same numbers. The archive can say the responses are the same, which it does; what it cannot say is how many times the coefficients are stored. The era prior leans one way and a prior may not close a claim.

alternatives.reading: The two types share a front end and nothing else -- the same pre-filter bolted to two different delay lines and two different modulators.

separated_by.observable: The modulation depth of both types read as a pitch excursion at the same settings of `40 03 07` Depth and `40 03 06` Rate, with the flanger's `40 03 08` at 64 so its loop is open. A flanger with no feedback and a chorus are the same arithmetic if the delay line and the modulator are shared, so the excursion in cents either matches at every depth setting or it does not.

predicts.one stage reached twice: The same excursion at every depth setting, to the vibrato reading's own repeats.
predicts.a shared front end only: Excursions that differ at some depth setting by more than one step of the depth byte is worth.

separated_by.divergence: One step of the depth byte, which on the types already read this way is several per cent of the excursion.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: The vibrato stage repeats an excursion to a few parts in a thousand on the records already published with it, which is well inside one step of the byte.

run.stimulus: a held tone, rate parked low enough to resolve the sweep

alternatives.reading: The flanger's extra parameter is a loop around the same delay line the chorus uses, which is the thing the two lists being one row apart suggests and the thing nothing here has measured.

separated_by.observable: The decay of the flanger's response at several settings of `40 03 08`, with the modulator parked so the delay is fixed. A loop around a delay of d milliseconds puts its resonances at multiples of 1/d and makes them sharper as the byte goes up; the pre-delay byte then moves those resonances by exactly what it moves the delay by, which is what says the loop is around that delay rather than around something else.

predicts.a loop around the shared delay: A comb whose spacing is one over the pre-delay setting, moving with the pre-delay byte and sharpening with the feedback byte.
predicts.a second structure of its own: Resonances that do not move with the pre-delay byte, or do not space themselves by it.

separated_by.divergence: The whole spacing of a comb, which at a pre-delay of a few milliseconds is hundreds of hertz.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: A twelfth-octave band set separates 0.0847 octaves, which at the frequencies a comb of this spacing puts its teeth is far finer than one tooth.

run.stimulus: the same held note, modulator parked, pre-delay asked at two values so the comb has to move

refuted_by: The two pre-filters departing at a setting neither run asked -- the grid is eleven of a hundred and twenty-eight through the low pass and four through the high pass, so a table that agreed at those and not between them would look exactly like this. Or either type's filter turning out to move with something the other's does not: both runs parked the modulator and opened the loop, and a pre-filter that depended on either would have been read at one point of a surface rather than as a curve.
what_it_would_change: Two of the sixty-four types stop being two front ends. One pre-filter section, one byte choosing between off, a low pass and a high pass, and one cutoff table, serve both -- and the cutoff table is the one the frequency class already closed.

It puts the question where it belongs. If the front ends are one section then what separates a chorus from a flanger on this unit is whatever the feedback byte reaches, and that is one run rather than a comparison of two whole types.
what_this_does_not_settle: The delay line. Nothing here read one: both runs parked the modulator and the pre-delay, which is what makes the filter comparison clean and is also what takes the delay out of it.
The modulator. The rate byte agrees on both, and that is a table nineteen types share and says nothing about these two.
What the feedback byte is around. That is the question the file is named after and it is the third alternative below, with its run.
Whether the front end is one section or two identical ones. No reading of this unit's output can tell those apart and the first alternative says so.
